title: Capacitance Defined: C = Q / V
welcome_lead: Store charge per volt and meet the farad — a surprisingly huge unit.
meta_desc: A-Level Capacitance adventure on definition of capacitance and parallel-plate basics.
final_note: Capacitance is geometry: bigger plates, smaller gap and a good dielectric all help.

concepts.def: Device storing energy in an electric field.
Charge stored per volt: C = Q / V.
Coulomb per volt; 1 F is very large.

walkthroughs.body_html: A capacitor's capacitance is the charge stored per volt across its terminals. C in farads, Q in coulombs, V in volts. Most practical caps are µF, nF or pF.
C = ε₀ ε_r A / d. Larger area or smaller separation increases C. A dielectric of permittivity ε_r boosts C by ε_r compared with vacuum.
Connecting to a battery moves charge until V_cap = V_supply. Then Q = CV. No further current flows in DC steady state.
